newsitem.title: LATVIA: SAVINGS BANK PUBLIC OFFER RULES DUE MARCH 20.
newsitem.headline: SAVINGS BANK PUBLIC OFFER RULES DUE MARCH 20.

text.p: The rules for the public offer of shares in state-owned Latvian Savings Bank (Krajbanka) will be decided tomorrow, March 20, the Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) said on Wednesday.
"It will be decided tomorrow how much of the 51 percent state stake of Savings Bank will be sold in the public offer," Viktor Shadinov, LPA legal manager, told a news conference.

He said that the privatisation agency has decided not to sell Savings Bank's shares for vouchers to employees in order not to reduce the number of shares in the public offer and not to bring up the price.
Savings Bank is the last major bank privatisation in Latvia after the government sold off shares in Unibanka, now quoted on the stock exchange.

Analysts say that foreign and local banks may be interested in taking part in the sale of Savings Bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has already expressed an interest.
The government owns 75 percent of Savings Bank but it is to keep some of the bank. Due to the EBRD interest, there will be for some time a government stake in Savings Bank, the LPA said.
The remaining 25 percent of Savings Bank is shared between three Ventspils companies and the SWH company plus other private investors.
